title: One federal programme, two routes into the same organization
question: How often does an organization’s audit show the same federal programme arriving through the City and by another route in the same year?
finding: Often, and mostly for an ordinary reason. 250 audit-year and programme pairs at City-paid organizations show money through the City and by another route; in 147 pairs at 32 organizations both sides are $100,000 or more. Most second routes are other counties or the State, for organizations that work in several places. In 21 pairs the second route is a direct federal award, as at Alzheimer's Association; Community Housing Partnership; Grid Alternatives Inc; Healthright 360; Heluna Health.
how: Award lines in each single audit grouped by federal assistance listing number and by route: direct from a federal agency, through the City, through a State body, or through another body. A pair is listed when the City route and the others together are each $100,000 or more in one audit year.
limits: Layered funding is how these programmes are built and is not double payment: a treatment provider serves several counties, a child-care agency holds a State contract and a City one, a housing operator has a direct federal grant for one building and a City-routed grant for another. The pattern matters only where one site or one staff team is charged to both routes, which the audit’s cost-allocation notes and the two grant budgets would show. No row here shows that. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
